songs.name: I've Been All Around This World

ai_show_review.summary: Acoustic Black Peter shines; Lovelight transition brightens chaotic set
ai_show_review.blurb: The Phoenix show is anchored by a superb acoustic Black Peter and an extended Not Fade Away → Turn On Your Lovelight segue. Pigpen’s guest vocals/harmonica add both amusement and annoyance to the latter part of the set, leaving the ending uneven.
ai_show_review.review: On March 8, 1970 at the Travelodge Theatre in the Round, the Dead delivered a tightly wound acoustic showcase that highlights Ron "Pigpen" McKernan’s soulful presence. Jerry’s vocals on Black Peter are described as “sweet, musical and heart‑breakingly passionate,” and his guitar work shines during the early numbers. Bob Weir’s voice remains crystal clear throughout, while the rhythm section stays “tight and solid.” The highlight of the night is the sprawling Not Fade Away → Turn On Your Lovelight transition, a moment that many reviewers cite as a high point. However, an on‑stage guest vocalist/harpist interrupts several songs, turning the final three numbers into a chaotic—if sometimes entertaining—culmination that some fans found “irritating” and others defended. The soundboard recordings capture the performance well; the recommended SBD (gd70-03-08.sbd.9195.sbeok.shnf) offers good clarity despite minor volume fluctuations, making it the most listenable version of this mixed‑quality but historically interesting show.

rating_calculation.sentiment_rationale: All three recordings label the sentiment as mixed, balancing praise for Black Peter and the Lovelight segue against criticism of the guest vocalist and uneven ending. No consistent positive or negative trend emerges, so no adjustment is applied.

best_recording.reason: Good soundboard capture with clear acoustic detail and the most complete set, despite minor volume fluctuations.

key_highlights: Stellar Black Peter performance with heartfelt vocals.
Extended Not Fade Away → Turn On Your Lovelight transition shines.
Guest vocalist/harpist adds chaotic but memorable atmosphere to final songs.
Tight, solid drumming keeps the set grounded.

band_performance.Jerry: Vocals sweet and heart‑breakingly passionate on Black Peter; guitar praised in acoustic sections.
band_performance.Bob: Voice crystal clear and strong throughout the show.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums tight and solid, providing a steady backbone.
